description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Initial Accuracy, Final Accuracy, and Δ Accuracy—for a large language model (LLM) under external feedback, as presented in the paper “Feedback Friction: LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback.” The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans from approximately 0.82 to 0.99 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, also on a linear scale, with major gridlines at 0.2 intervals. The “Initial Accuracy” (green dashed line with square markers) begins near 0.55 at an initial confidence of 0.82, fluctuates slightly, then rises steadily to approximately 0.98 at 0.99. The “Final Accuracy” (blue solid line with circle markers) starts near 1.0 at 0.82, dips slightly to around 0.98 at 0.84, then remains relatively stable with minor fluctuations, ending near 0.99 at 0.99. The “Δ Accuracy” (orange dashed line with diamond markers), representing the change in accuracy after feedback, begins near 0.5 at 0.82, drops sharply to about 0.35 at 0.86, then rises to a peak of approximately 0.75 at 0.93 before declining again to around 0.65 at 0.99. Error bars are present for all three lines, indicating variability in the measurements.
